findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 5
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - A host’s process access policy prevents both `ps` and `kill -0` from inspecting a still-running worker. This fallback treats every `kill -0` failure as proof that the process has ended, but [Linux kill(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/kill.2.html) also reports failure when permission is denied. Confirmed turn-off can therefore delete the active worker’s folder. The previous code treated a permission failure as still running, so the earlier process-identity finding remains open.
